concept: Pull SCVs immediately at game start for the fastest possible worker attack, relying on group cohesion, focus fire, and repairs rather than any economy or infrastructure.
rules: Check emergency_defence first, then immediate_assault. Otherwise use immediate_assault, sustain_or_end.
Start moving at once with up to ten SCVs; do not wait to train workers, build supply, or gather a normal economic lead.
Keep attacking SCVs together, use a repair group for low-health workers, and do not donate isolated SCVs to enemy defenders.
This is the most committed worker rush. It has no intended macro recovery if it fails to gain a decisive advantage.

enter_when: The game has started and the initial SCV group is crossing the map or beginning its first fight.
phases.goal: Create the earliest possible worker engagement.
guidance: Immediately send up to ten SCVs to the enemy base and keep them compact.
Target exposed workers and weak units first.
If an enemy wall is closed, wait for an opening or attack targets outside it rather than feeding into the choke.
Use healthy workers to fight and surround while damaged workers move behind for repair.

enter_when: The initial worker clash has resolved into continued pressure, a possible base kill, or a stalled attack.
phases.goal: Finish a winning attack or preserve the remaining workers from a lost one.
guidance: If the worker line is collapsing, keep SCVs together and finish workers, production, and the town hall by accessibility.
If defenders can win the local fight, preserve retreating workers rather than feeding reinforcements.
Use any later Marines as reinforcement but do not delay the worker attack waiting for them.

enter_when: A direct counterattack would end the game before the worker rush succeeds.
phases.goal: Choose the action most likely to avoid or deliver immediate defeat.
guidance: Bring back only workers required to prevent immediate loss; otherwise keep the pressure group committed.
If both bases are exposed, favor the action most likely to end the game immediately rather than beginning normal macro.
